title: In, At and On: Location Expressions
summary: Use in, on and at in common location expressions for queues, departments, pictures, floors, lists, directions, building positions and corners. Distinguish the interior, endpoint and surface perspectives involved in these expressions.
learningObjectives: Use in with rows, queues, pictures, departments, newspapers, the sky and the countryside.
Use on with floors, left/right positions, maps, lists, websites, coastlines and travel routes.
Use at with the top, bottom and end of a place or object, and choose suitable phrases for the front or back.
Distinguish in the corner of a room from at/on the corner of a street, and in a car from at a building’s front.

explanation.heading: In: groups, images, publications and wider environments
explanation.body: Use in with a line, a queue, a row, a department and an office, as well as with people or things represented in a photograph. Printed material can be in a newspaper, magazine or book. Other fixed combinations include in the sky, in the world and in the country when it means outside towns and cities.
explanation.example: The journalist recognised her colleague in the newspaper photograph.

explanation.heading: On: sides, floors, lists, routes and geographical edges
explanation.body: Use on the left/right for positions, on the third floor for a level in a building, and on a list, menu, map, page or website for information presented there. Towns may lie on a river, on a road or on the coast. A stop made during a journey is on the way.
explanation.example: The workshop is on the first floor, on your left as you leave the lift.

explanation.heading: At: the top, bottom and end of a defined area
explanation.body: Use at the top, at the bottom and at the end when locating something at a boundary or endpoint. The expression often includes of plus the place or object: at the top of the stairs or at the end of the corridor. Do not replace at with in just because the overall place is enclosed.
explanation.example: You will find the emergency exit at the end of the corridor.

explanation.heading: Front and back depend on the kind of space
explanation.body: Passengers sit in the front or in the back of a car because these are interior areas. Visitors may stand at the front or at the back of a theatre, hall or group, indicating a region of that place. An address written on the back of an envelope appears on its surface.
explanation.example: I sat in the back of the car and later stood at the front of the hall.

explanation.heading: Corners: inside a room versus a street junction
explanation.body: A plant in the corner of a room occupies a corner within an enclosed space. A shop at the corner or on the corner of a street is located at a road junction; both at and on can be natural there. The distinction follows the location being described, not just the word corner.
explanation.example: A reading lamp stands in the corner of the room, and a bakery is on the corner of the street.

comparisons.title: Interior seating versus a region of a public venue

left.label: In the back of a car
left.example: The child sat in the back of the car.
left.note: In identifies an interior seating area.

right.label: At the back of a venue
right.example: We stood at the back of the auditorium.
right.note: At identifies the rear section of a large venue.

left.label: In the corner of a room
left.example: The recycling bin is in the corner of the office.
left.note: The bin occupies part of the room interior.

right.label: At/on the corner of a street
right.example: There is a pharmacy on the corner of the street.
right.note: The shop is located at a street junction.

comparisons.title: Something printed inside versus on its exterior

left.label: In a magazine
left.example: I read the article in a magazine.
left.note: The article is part of the publication.

right.label: On a card
right.example: The address is on the back of the card.
right.note: The words appear on a physical surface.

comparisons.title: Information on a list versus a person in a queue

left.label: On a list
left.example: The visitor’s name is on the registration list.
left.note: A written entry belongs on the list.

right.label: In a queue
right.example: The visitor is standing in a queue.
right.note: The person is part of the group waiting in line.

examples.sentence: All six dancers stood in a row for the photograph.
examples.note: In a row describes an arrangement of people.

examples.sentence: The design team works in the research department.
examples.note: In is conventional when naming a department.

examples.sentence: You can find the updated policy on the organisation’s website.
examples.note: Electronic information published on a website takes on.

examples.sentence: The café is on the coast, a few kilometres south of the harbour.
examples.note: On the coast describes a location along the coastline.

examples.sentence: Write the document number at the bottom of the form.
examples.note: At the bottom of locates a detail at a defined boundary.

examples.sentence: I was sitting in the front of the taxi, next to the driver.
examples.note: In marks a seating area within the vehicle.

examples.sentence: There is a small bookshop at the corner of Oak Street.
examples.note: At the corner identifies a street junction; on the corner could also be natural.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Her office is in the fifth floor.
commonMistakes.correct: Her office is on the fifth floor.
commonMistakes.why: Building levels are described with on the ... floor.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The person in the back row is not on the photograph.
commonMistakes.correct: The person in the back row is not in the photograph.
commonMistakes.why: People represented in an image are in the photograph.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Write your email address in the top of the form.
commonMistakes.correct: Write your email address at the top of the form.
commonMistakes.why: At the top of identifies a boundary or edge of the form.

commonMistakes.incorrect: A flowerpot stands at the corner of our living room.
commonMistakes.correct: A flowerpot stands in the corner of our living room.
commonMistakes.why: In the corner describes a location inside a room; at the corner is more usual for a junction or external point.

studyTips: Make two columns of conventional expressions: in a queue / in a picture / in the sky and on a floor / on a list / on the left.
Sketch a car, a theatre and an envelope; label in the back, at the back and on the back, respectively.
Compare an object in the corner of a room with a shop at the corner of a street; practise the difference aloud.

exercises.prompt: Our project team has moved to an office ___ the fourth floor of the building.
exercises.feedback: Use on with numbered floors in a building.

exercises.prompt: You can see my younger brother ___ this family photograph, beside our grandparents.
exercises.feedback: People who appear in a photograph are in the photograph.

exercises.prompt: Please put your initials ___ the bottom of the application form.
exercises.feedback: At the bottom of identifies the lower boundary of the document.

exercises.prompt: There was a small plant ___ the corner of the classroom, next to the window.
exercises.feedback: In the corner of a room describes a position within that enclosed space.

exercises.prompt: The instructions for the event are available ___ . (our website; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: on our website
exercises.feedback: We normally say information is on a website.

exercises.prompt: Four people were waiting ___ . (a queue; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: in a queue
exercises.feedback: People waiting together stand in a queue.

exercises.prompt: The fishing village is ___ . (the west coast; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: on the west coast
exercises.feedback: On the coast describes a location along a coastline.

exercises.prompt: There were no clouds ___ . (the sky; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: in the sky
exercises.feedback: In the sky is the conventional expression for something visible above us.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: Please write the reference number in the back of the envelope.
acceptedAnswers: Please write the reference number on the back of the envelope.
exercises.feedback: Writing on the exterior surface of an envelope takes on.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: I saw your picture on the magazine, printed next to the interview.
acceptedAnswers: I saw your picture in the magazine, printed next to the interview.
exercises.feedback: A picture published inside a magazine is in the magazine; on suggests its exterior surface.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: The teacher asked us to wait on a queue outside the classroom.
acceptedAnswers: The teacher asked us to wait in a queue outside the classroom.
exercises.feedback: People waiting in line are in a queue.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: You will find our customer support team on the service department.
acceptedAnswers: You will find our customer support team in the service department.
exercises.feedback: Departments are organisational spaces normally introduced with in.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use the details in one sentence: the laboratory / be / on / the third floor. Begin with “The laboratory”.
acceptedAnswers: The laboratory is on the third floor.
The laboratory's on the third floor.
speakingExercises.feedback: On marks the building floor where the laboratory is located.

speakingExercises.prompt: A colleague asks where your surname appears. State the fact in one sentence: my surname / be / on the list. Begin with “My surname”.
acceptedAnswers: My surname is on the list.
My surname's on the list.
speakingExercises.feedback: An entry appears on a written list.

speakingExercises.prompt: Turn these facts into one sentence: six visitors / wait / in a queue / yesterday. Begin with “Six visitors” and use the past continuous.
acceptedAnswers: Six visitors were waiting in a queue yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: In a queue is the standard expression for people waiting in line.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition, and say the whole sentence: “The notice is in the top of the page.”
acceptedAnswers: The notice is at the top of the page.
speakingExercises.feedback: At the top of identifies the upper boundary of the page.

speakingExercises.prompt: Compare two places in one sentence. Facts: a lamp / be / in the corner of the room; a café / be / on the corner of the street. Begin with “The lamp” and join with “and”.
acceptedAnswers: The lamp is in the corner of the room, and the café is on the corner of the street.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use in for a room interior and on for a street junction.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks where you sat in a car. Answer with one complete sentence beginning “I sat” and using “in the back of the car”.
acceptedAnswers: I sat in the back of the car.
speakingExercises.feedback: In the back describes an interior seating position.

speakingExercises.prompt: Produce exactly two sentences. First: the visitors / stand / at the front of the hall. Second: the event schedule / appear / on the website. Use present simple, and begin with “The visitors” and “The event schedule”.
acceptedAnswers: The visitors stand at the front of the hall. The event schedule appears on the website.
speakingExercises.feedback: At the front describes a region of the hall; on a website describes published information.

speakingExercises.prompt: You are giving directions inside an office. Say one sentence using these facts: the meeting room / be / on your left. Begin with “The meeting room”.
acceptedAnswers: The meeting room is on your left.
The meeting room's on your left.
speakingExercises.feedback: On your left is the usual directional expression.

listeningExercises.audioText: Your appointment is on the second floor. When you leave the lift, turn right to find the office.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where should the visitor look for the office?
listeningExercises.feedback: The appointment is on the second floor, with directions from the lift.

listeningExercises.audioText: I recognised the actor in a newspaper photograph, but their name was missing from the article.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did the speaker see the actor?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker recognised the actor in a photograph printed in the newspaper.

listeningExercises.audioText: The receptionist asked everyone to wait in a queue near the entrance.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word location expression immediately after “wait”.
acceptedAnswers: in a queue
listeningExercises.feedback: In a queue locates people within the line of those waiting.

listeningExercises.audioText: I sat in the back of the car, while my brother drove and Mum sat beside him.
choices: In the rear of the car.
At the back of the theatre.
On the roof of the car.
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker sat in the back of the car, an interior seating area.

listeningExercises.audioText: At the end of the hallway you will find a small door that leads directly into the garden.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where is the garden door located?
choices: At the start of the hallway.
At the far end of the hallway.
In the middle of the stairs.
listeningExercises.feedback: At the end of the hallway places the door at that corridor’s endpoint.

listeningExercises.audioText: We stopped at a bakery on the way to the coast, then continued driving until sunset.
listeningExercises.prompt: When did the travellers stop at the bakery?
choices: During their journey to the coast.
listeningExercises.feedback: On the way to the coast means the stop happened during that journey.

listeningExercises.audioText: The teacher wrote her name at the top of the attendance sheet.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word location expression immediately after “name”.
acceptedAnswers: at the top of
listeningExercises.feedback: At the top of points to the upper edge of the sheet.

listeningExercises.audioText: The new café stands on the corner of Elm Street.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word location expression immediately after “stands”.
acceptedAnswers: on the corner of
listeningExercises.feedback: On the corner of identifies a location at a street junction.
